name: FM24C64B-GTR
title: FM24C64B: 64 Kbit (8K x 8) I2C serial F-RAM, 4.5 V to 5.5 V
summary: A 64 Kbit nonvolatile ferroelectric RAM organised as 8192 bytes, reached over a two-wire I2C bus at up to 1 MHz from a 4.5 V to 5.5 V supply. Each byte is stored as soon as its eighth bit arrives, so there is no write cycle to wait out and no acknowledge polling; a write can be followed at once by any other operation. It shares the pinout of an 8-pin serial EEPROM, with three address pins for up to eight devices on one bus and a WP pin that locks the whole array. FM24C64B-GTR is the 8-pin SOIC part on tape and reel, industrial range -40 °C to +85 °C.
key_figures: I2C, SCL up to 1 MHz (also 100 kHz and 400 kHz timings)
none; bytes are written at bus speed
100 µA max at 100 kHz, 200 µA max at 400 kHz, 400 µA max at 1 MHz
10 years at 85 °C, 38 years at 75 °C, 151 years at 65 °C (min)

notes: Order code fields: FM = Cypress; 24 = I2C F-RAM; C = voltage, 4.5 V to 5.5 V; 64 = density, 64 Kbit; B = die revision; G = package, 8-pin SOIC; option blank = standard, TR = tape and reel.
Both parts are Pb-free and RoHS compliant.

pins.name: A0
pins.function: Device select address bit 0. With A1 and A2 it must equal bits 3-1 of the slave address byte for the device to respond, so eight devices can share a bus. Internal pull-down.

pins.name: A1
pins.function: Device select address bit 1; see A0. Internal pull-down.

pins.name: A2
pins.function: Device select address bit 2; see A0. Internal pull-down.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: Bidirectional serial address and data line. Open-drain output with slope-controlled falling edge; Schmitt-trigger input. Requires a pull-up resistor to the supply and may be wired-AND with the rest of the bus.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: Serial clock, Schmitt-trigger input. Data enters on the rising edge and leaves on the falling edge.

pins.name: WP
pins.function: Write protect. High (VDD) protects every address; low (ground) allows writes everywhere. Internal pull-down.

circuits.title: Several FM24C64B on one I2C bus with a microcontroller
circuits.description: A microcontroller drives SCL and SDA, each pulled up to VDD by one resistor, and up to eight FM24C64B hang on the two lines. Each memory gets its own address by how its A2-A0 pins are strapped: device #0 has all three at ground, #1 has A0 at VDD, #7 has all three at VDD. WP is grounded on every device so the whole array can be written. The pull-up value lies between RPmin and RPmax from the two equations.
notes: Devices #2 to #6 sit on the same SDA and SCL lines with the remaining A2-A0 codes.
Each memory's VDD pin goes to the supply and its VSS pin to ground.

operation.text: 8,192 locations of one byte each. A location is chosen by a 13-bit address sent as two bytes; the top three bits of the high byte are ignored. Memory access takes no time beyond the serial transfer itself.

The FM24C64B is only ever a slave: the bus master makes the clock for every operation. A START is SDA falling while SCL is high; a STOP is SDA rising while SCL is high. Every command opens with a START and should close with a STOP. A START at any moment aborts what is in progress and leaves the part ready for a new command, and a STOP during an operation also aborts it. Outside START and STOP, SDA may change only while SCL is low.
If VDD has fallen below its minimum during operation, the master should send a START before the next operation.

After every eighth bit the transmitter lets go of SDA and the receiver pulls it low on the ninth clock to acknowledge. SDA left high (no-acknowledge) ends the operation; after a failed byte this lets the master readdress the part and repeat the last byte. On a read the master must not acknowledge the final byte it wants, otherwise the memory tries to drive the next byte just as the master tries to send STOP or a new command.

The first byte after a START: bits 7-4 hold the type code 1010b, bits 3-1 must equal the levels on A2, A1, A0, and bit 0 is R/W (1 = read, 0 = write). Up to eight FM24C64B can share one bus, each with a different A2-A0 code. All bytes travel MSB first.

An internal latch holds the current address: the last one written, or the one after the last byte accessed. It is advanced just before the acknowledge of every data byte, wraps from 1FFFh to 0000h, and keeps its value while power stays up. Reads always start at the current address. A transfer may run for any number of bytes.

Slave address with R/W = 0, two address bytes, then any number of data bytes, each acknowledged. A byte is stored once its eighth bit is in, before the acknowledge, so a write is finished by the time the next transfer can start: there is no page buffer, no write cycle time, and acknowledge polling always shows ready. To abandon a byte without changing memory, send START or STOP before its eighth bit.
WP high (VDD) protects the whole array: data bytes sent to it get no acknowledge and the address counter does not advance. WP low (VSS) allows writes. WP has an internal pull-down.

Slave address with R/W = 1; on the following clock the part begins sending the byte at the latched address. Each byte the master acknowledges is followed by the next one, wrapping from 1FFFh to 0000h.

Send the slave address with R/W = 0 and the two address bytes to load the latch, then a repeated START (which drops the write) and the slave address with R/W = 1. From there it is a current address read.

Four ways end a read cleanly: no-acknowledge on the 9th clock and STOP on the 10th (the preferred one); no-acknowledge on the 9th and START on the 10th; STOP on the 9th; or START on the 9th. Anything else will probably leave the memory and the master both driving the bus.

Every read restores the data it reads, so reads count against endurance as writes do. Each access cycles a whole 64-bit row, and a new row begins at every 8-byte boundary; spreading busy data over different rows stretches endurance. At 3000 accesses per second to one segment it takes 10 years to reach 10^12 cycles.

Wait at least tPU = 10 ms after VDD passes its minimum before the first START. VDD may drop below its minimum immediately after the last STOP (tPD = 0). VDD must ramp no faster than 30 µs/V both up and down.

SCL and SDA inputs have Schmitt triggers; the noise suppression time constant tSP on SCL and SDA is 50 ns max. A0-A2 and WP each have an internal pull-down of 40 kΩ below VIL that weakens to 1 MΩ above VIH.
Pin-compatible with 8-pin I2C serial EEPROMs and able to run the 100 kHz and 400 kHz bus timings as well as 1 MHz.
